No. 

While the dialogue mostly unfolds in "real-time," there are jarring, illogical jumps in the story's timeline (inappropriate compression of time) that disrupt the pacing and continuity. 

Specifically, Leon walks into the café and sits down, and in the very next sentence, the stage directions state that "they both stir their cups"—skipping entirely over how or when Leon ordered and received his coffee. Furthermore, at the end of the very brief conversation (which takes less than two minutes to read and contains no indication of a time-lapse), Leon asks Mara if she wants *another* coffee, even though the earlier stage directions explicitly noted they hadn't even taken a drink from their first cups yet. Because the story is written as a continuous, real-time scene, compressing the time it takes to order, receive, and finish a hot beverage into non-existent gaps between consecutive lines of dialogue feels unbalanced and unintentional.
